subject: environmental-science
title: Montreal Protocol Success
welcome_lead: 1987 Montreal — humanity's most successful environmental treaty.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on the Montreal Protocol and ozone recovery.
final_note: Universal ratification + clear science + viable substitutes = success worth remembering.

concepts.def: 1987 treaty phasing out ozone-depleting substances; universally ratified.
Hydrofluorocarbons; CFC substitutes with no Cl but high GWP.
Hydrochlorofluorocarbons; transitional substitutes with reduced ODP.
Finance mechanism helping developing countries comply (~$4.5 bn since 1991).

walkthroughs.body_html: The Protocol's stepwise schedules and amendments allowed scientific updates. London 1990, Copenhagen 1992 accelerated CFC phaseout.
WMO/UNEP 2022: Antarctic ozone projected to recover to 1980 levels by ~2066; mid-latitudes by ~2040.
Without Montreal, CFCs would have added ~0.5°C warming by 2050. Kigali HFC phasedown avoids ~0.4°C more.
